title: ISO weeks; `dayofweek` from Sunday; `date_trunc('week')` to Monday; floors before 1970
verdict: ISO `weekofyear`, `YEAROFWEEK`, `DOW_ISO`; `dayofweek` 1 = Sunday; floor before the epoch
description: `weekofyear` and `extract(WEEK …)` are ISO weeks (2021-01-03 is week 53 of 2020), `extract(YEAROFWEEK …)` the ISO year, `extract(DOW_ISO …)` 1 = Monday … 7 = Sunday. `dayofweek` and `extract(DOW …)` count 1 = Sunday … 7 = Saturday, and `weekday` 0 = Monday … 6 = Sunday. `date_trunc('week', …)` and `trunc(d, 'week')` go back to Monday.

Before 1970 parts and truncations floor: `date_trunc('second', 1969-12-31 23:59:59.5)` is 23:59:59, `extract(SECOND …)` 59.500000 (a decimal). `datediff` counts days; `timestampdiff(MONTH, 2024-01-31, 2024-02-29)` is 0, whole months only.

`date_format` and `to_date` take Java `DateTimeFormatter` patterns; the week-based letters (`Y`, `w`, `u`, `e`) raise `INCONSISTENT_BEHAVIOR_CROSS_VERSION` in both modes. Spark has no `date_bin`; `window(ts, '5 minutes')` buckets from the epoch.
reference: `date_part` and `date_trunc` (`Time.lean`): ISO weeks, Monday-based `isodow`, flooring before the epoch; `strftime` is opaque. Spark is native for the ISO parts; `dayofweek` is a different numbering a writer maps.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_spark` runs each query four times on one local session: with `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` true and false, on the folded path (the optimizer evaluates a query over `VALUES` on the driver) and on the codegen path (`ConvertToLocalRelation` and `ConstantFolding` excluded, so the query runs as a job with whole-stage code generation). probes.json keeps one result per ANSI setting where the two paths agree. Spark 4.3.0 (pyspark 4.3.0), Java 21.0.12, Linux x86_64, `local[2]`, session time zone UTC, `spark.sql.timestampType=TIMESTAMP_NTZ`.
